evidence.title: NCLT or RERA - Who to Approach for Possession | Understanding Real Estate Regulatories
evidence.property_name: NCLT or RERA - Who to Approach for Possession | Understanding Real Estate Regulatories
evidence.description: With the implementation of the RERA Act, 2016, the builders are liable to disclose every detail of the project they have registered on the RERA website. They need to provide updated information regularly to the buyers. RERA emphasizes timely completion and possession of the projects. The home buyers can register the case of delayed possession or fraudulency with RERA. Based on the offense or non-compliance, RERA penalizes the promoter or the builder. The penalty can be monetary or imprisonment. ## Compensation from the builder under RERA [...] ## Compensation from the builder under RERA According to Section 18 of the RERA Act, the allottee(s) has the option of continuing with the project or suing the builder for compensation for the delayed possession of the apartment or building. It allows the allottees to seek compensation from the builder for the number of days delayed in handing over the possession. ## Steps to seek compensation from the builder via RERA [...] Therefore, while buying the property, ensure you carefully read the sale agreement before signing. You should also check all the property-related documents carefully to avoid fraudulence and to remain on the safe side. ## Conclusion to RERA / NCLT RERA and NCLT are the government setups to protect the interests of the buyers of the property. In case of delayed possession from the date mentioned by the builder, homebuyers can take help from RERA or NCLT. Homebuyers can make a complaint with RERA online or offline by getting help from the Adjudicating Officer. You can also register your complaint with NCLT. The homebuyers can either seek compensation for the delayed possession certificate or get a refund and withdraw interest from the project.
